I fixed the typo with a new migration and left `0007_add_customers.sql` untouched. The project's memory store has a rule that files in `migrations/` are already applied in production and must never be edited. If I had changed 0007 directly, production would never pick up the fix, and new environments would end up with a different schema from production.

The new file is `migrations/0008_fix_customers_email.sql`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;
```

I haven't run it. `RENAME COLUMN` works on Postgres, SQLite 3.25+ and MySQL 8+. Nothing else in the repo refers to `emial`, so no code needs updating.

If 0007 has never actually been applied anywhere, it would be simpler to edit it directly and delete 0008. Tell me if that's the case and I'll switch it over.
